## 📥 How to install this

**Scroll down to "Assets" and pick the file for your computer.**

| Your computer | Download this file |
| --- | --- |
| **Mac** (any Mac — Intel or Apple Silicon) | the file ending in **`.dmg`** |
| **Windows** | **`Generate4U-Setup.exe`** |

*The other files in the list are used by the app to update itself. You don't need them.*

---

### ⚠️ Your computer will warn you about this app. That's expected.

Generate4U is a small school tool, not commercial software, so it isn't registered
with Apple or Microsoft. Both systems show a warning for any app that isn't. **The
warning is about the absence of a paid certificate — it is not a virus alert, and it
does not mean anything is wrong with the app.** All of the code is public on this page
for your IT team to check.

Here's how to get past it.

### On a Mac

1. Open the downloaded **`.dmg`** file.
2. **Drag "WHS IEP BSP Generator" into the Applications folder.**
   (That's the app's original internal name — it's the right one.)
3. Open it from Applications. Your Mac will say it *"could not verify"* the app, or
   that it's from an *"unidentified developer"*. Then:
   - **macOS 15 (Sequoia) and newer:** click **Done**. Open
     **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down to the message about
     Generate4U, and click **Open Anyway**. Confirm **Open Anyway** again.
   - **Older macOS:** in Applications, **right-click** (or Control-click) the app →
     **Open** → **Open**. A plain double-click won't offer this option; you must
     right-click the first time.
4. After that first time, it opens normally like any other app.

> **This warning comes back after every update.** Each new download is treated as a
> brand-new app by macOS, so expect to repeat step 3 each time you update. Annoying,
> but harmless and expected.

### On Windows

1. Open the downloaded **`Generate4U-Setup.exe`**.
2. Windows may show a blue box: **"Windows protected your PC"**. Click **More info**,
   then **Run anyway**.
3. There's no setup wizard — a short animation plays and the app opens by itself,
   with shortcuts added to your Start menu and desktop.
4. Updates install themselves quietly from then on. You won't see this warning again.

---

### If your school network blocks the download

Ask your IT team to allow **`github.com`**. On Windows, automatic updates also need
**`update.electronjs.org`**, so it's worth mentioning both at once.

### Your privacy

Everything you type stays on your computer. Documents and progress files save locally
and nothing you write is ever uploaded. The app's only internet use is checking
whether a newer version exists — no student information is ever sent.

### Can't install software on your computer?

There's a browser version that needs no installation at all — see
**[the README](https://github.com/jacknolanedu/whs-iep-bsp-generator#no-install-allowed-use-the-browser-version)**.
